answer: Coordination-priced admission. Each identity pays a fee equal to the current total number of active identities touching its declared coordination group, so joining a fresh vine costs little but merging into a busy group costs proportionally more. Attacker forging N sybils in one group pays sum over joins of group size, roughly N²/2 units; splitting across a wide mesa of groups keeps per-group size low but forces many costly separate voyages of coordination proof, and each group's fee rises as it grows, so scaling sybils linearly costs quadratically overall.
